long_biography.plain_text:
Mechanical work with his father introduced John Rosatti to the practical skills he later carried into automotive retail. After jobs moving and dismantling cars, he opened a Brooklyn body shop in 1968, then acquired Honda motorcycle and Oldsmobile operations. He developed those beginnings into Plaza Auto Mall, combining several vehicle brands under one dealership group.

Rosatti managed the business hands-on, overseeing its individual operating units as it expanded beyond New York. In 2024, Rosatti/Plaza Auto Group comprised seven dealerships and continued to identify him as president and top executive. The group remained a substantial multibrand automotive retailer under his leadership more than five decades after its Brooklyn formation.

uncertainties.detail: A mirrored old encyclopedia entry gives 1 March 1944, and that date is compatible with the source record's calculated age of 76 on 7 May 2020. No authoritative biography located in this pass confirms it, so no day, month or year is proposed.

A first-person Flickr profile states Brooklyn, New York, and the official biography says Rosatti was raised in Brooklyn. Because the Flickr account is not directly linked from the official personal site and the official wording does not explicitly locate his birth, no place-of-birth proposal is made.

Rosatti's official pages conflict on whether Plaza Auto Mall opened in 1972 or followed vehicle-business acquisitions described as occurring in 1976. The biographies retain the well-supported sequence without assigning a precise Plaza opening year.

Rosatti's personal history supports a founder-built automotive fortune, but family finances and other starting conditions are not documented in enough depth to distinguish an independent from an advantaged start. Broad Self-made is retained.

Rosatti founded BurgerFi and later held its securities through a revocable family trust for which he exercised voting and investment power. The filing does not convert trust-held shares into direct personal title, and later changes to BurgerFi do not alter the automotive origin of his fortune.

Restaurants, property and securities investments are documented, but their current aggregate value is not disclosed. The latest authoritative comparative evidence identifies the automotive group as a substantial seven-dealership business, making Automotive the strongest current classification.

The existing LinkedIn profile is identity-verified and the personal website is proposed. The Flickr page matches several facts but lacks a direct official cross-link, so it is retained as a research source rather than proposed as a social profile. No Instagram account was verified.

Private-family trivia, allegations, controversies, legal disputes and vessel-specific research were excluded. Family references were retained only where they materially explain early mechanical formation or the legal form of a trust-held investment.

review.notes: Identity and the Automotive creation and primary-industry classifications are very high confidence.
